fichas.title: Thermal insulation construction methods
fichas.summary: Compares traditional construction without a vapour barrier, warm-roof and warm-façade construction with vapour barriers, and construction with rear-ventilated outer skins. Describes layer arrangements, condensation risks, ventilation requirements, and precautions for insulated façades.
uses: Reduce heat transfer through walls and roofs
Ventilate rear-ventilated cladding and roof assemblies

dimensions.label: Minimum air-gap width for panel-like external skin
dimensions.ocr_raw: The width of the air gap with panel-like external skin amounts to min. 20 mm

dimensions.label: Minimum air-gap width for brickwork outer skin
dimensions.ocr_raw: or for brickwork outer skin min. 40 mm.

dimensions.label: Minimum fall between air inlet and outlet
dimensions.ocr_raw: Functional ventilation requires a height difference (minimum fall 10%) between air inlet and outlet.

fichas.title: Thermal bridges and condensation
fichas.summary: Thermal bridges are parts of building elements with less thermal insulation than surrounding areas. They can lower internal surface temperatures and cause condensation. The page illustrates condensation at corners and junctions and describes ways to improve internal surface temperatures; it also explains how surface-area relationships affect heat loss and condensation risk.
uses: Identify thermal bridges in building elements
Reduce condensation and mould risk at internal surfaces
Improve internal surface temperatures at corners and junctions
